cuts.item: Eight positions (school) plus four part-time tutors transferred
Further 17 positions: teachers, guidance counselors, secretary, reading specialist, special ed, custodians, maintenance worker, Title One coordinator
11.7 additional teachers, assistant principal, instructional coach, four part-time custodians, two maintenance people, three part-time secretaries, one full-time secretary
School IT contracted hours cut in half

statements.statement: Preliminary balanced budget revenue total stated by the town manager.
Recommended school increase of 2.94%, which does not meet any presented school scenario.
Governor's proposal reduces state aid because the town lost 40s smart growth funding.
Chapter 70 rising 1.56% in the governor's proposal; unrestricted aid up 3%.
Free cash used for capital items, OPEB and stabilization, not operating expenses.
Maximum levy stated, including prior base, 2.5% increase, new growth estimate and existing exclusions.
Superintendent's level service and Esser-removal budgets were 1.8 million and 1.2 million above the 2.5% budget; only an override could close that.
Override would require select board to place ballot question; warrant closes March 18th.
statements.who: the town manager and the chair

statements.statement: Active health insurance rate up 5.7%, retirees 6%.

warnings.condition: if there is no increase in revenue sources
warnings.prediction: Spending free cash year over year will erode it until none remains and capital projects are lost.
Town may face a similar situation next year with the health insurance buffer gone.
Pledged to defeat the town manager's budget at town meeting.
